objects.original: O in O(n), real symmetric A_O from (4), and v in R^n.
objects.reconstructed: Real orthogonal subtype, literal singleBlockPrecision, real coordinate function v:Fin n->Real, and IsHermitian over Real.
objects.evidence: Fin n coordinates represent R^n; real Hermitianity is symmetry, explicitly converted by Matrix.isHermitian_iff_isSymm. The current English statement and formulas use these same objects.

domains.original: Section 3.1 has kappa>=4 and 3<=n<=d; B.3 through (26) treats one block O(n) and all real vectors.
domains.reconstructed: n>=3,kappa>=4, every real orthogonal O, every real coordinate vector. No ambient d.
domains.evidence: n<=d controls fitting blocks into ambient dimension and is absent from the single-block proof. Every n>=3 can occur with d=n. The English lesson clearly labels its isolated single-block claim.

quantifiers.original: Every O and every v satisfy both bounds for the same A_O.
quantifiers.reconstructed: For all n>=3,kappa>=4,O, symmetry and forall v, both quadratic inequalities.
quantifiers.evidence: The universal vector quantifier includes zero and never chooses a different A. No nonzero-vector, genericity or determinant-sign restriction is added.

assumptions.original: Orthogonality, Equation (4), and the standing n,kappa range; Cauchy-Schwarz is part of the proof.
assumptions.reconstructed: Only 3<=n,4<=kappa and O:orthogonalGroup are theorem inputs.
assumptions.evidence: horth,hiso,hcs,hcross,htranspose,hexpand and hc are derived inside the proof. The English steps expressly identify internally derived estimates. The unused n bound retains the source lower bound rather than adding a claim.

conclusion.original: Symmetry plus ||v||_2^2<=v^T A_O v<=kappa||v||_2^2 for all v; equivalently the Loewner inequalities (26).
conclusion.reconstructed: Real Hermitianity and v dot v<=v dot(A v)<=kappa*(v dot v) for all v.
conclusion.evidence: Universal real quadratic inequalities together with symmetry are precisely the Loewner bounds. The English statement calls this a quadratic-form formulation. Coordinate square sums give the Euclidean square, with no Pi-norm or entrywise-order substitution.

scopes.original: The B.3 paragraph through (26) is one step toward the larger Lemma B.8, whose later conclusions concern the assembled matrix and minimizer.
scopes.reconstructed: Symmetry and quadratic bounds for one block only.
scopes.evidence: The English lesson title and source scope identify single-block bounds and explicitly exclude full Lemma 3.4/B.8. No assembled matrix membership, potential minimum or minimizer is advertised.

constant_dependencies.original: The exact constants 1 and kappa arise from (kappa+1)/2 plus or minus (kappa-1)/2.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: Identical constants, independent of dimension or O.
constant_dependencies.evidence: The final English step correctly uses the nonnegative (kappa-1)/2, substitutes the upper cross bound for the lower quadratic bound and vice versa, and displays the exact two coefficient identities.

deltas.description: Ambient d and n<=d are eliminated for the isolated single-block theorem; this is not a strengthened assumption or full-block conclusion.
deltas.evidence: The source proof through (26) uses no d; choose d=n to realize any n>=3. The English lesson consistently claims only a single block.
